THE DOOR: POST /attest takes one checkpoint from a registered store; GET /attest/key returns V3's witness public key and kid; GET /attest/<store>/<seq> returns the receipt V3 gave for that sequence, or 404. A store is a name V3 has registered with a public key; it carries no other identity, and the name may be opaque. The door verifies no claim and makes no verdict: it witnesses a head. The routes, the bytes and the rules are written in docs/WITNESS.md, which an integrator in any language can build from alone.

THE BYTES, exact and the same in every language. The store signs, with Ed25519, the UTF-8 bytes 'concordance-attest/v1' LF store LF seq LF head LF at LF, where store matches [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,62}, seq is a decimal integer from 1 to 2**53 with no sign or leading zero, head is 64 lowercase hex, and at is UTC as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. The request is JSON {store, seq, head, at, sig}, sig base64url without padding. V3 signs, with its issuer key, the bytes 'concordance-witness/v1' LF store LF seq LF head LF at LF witnessed_at LF prev LF, where witnessed_at is V3's UTC time in the same form and prev is the hash of this store's previous receipt or the word genesis. The receipt is JSON {format, store, seq, head, at, witnessed_at, prev, hash, kid, sig}: hash is the SHA-256 hex of those bytes and sig is V3's Ed25519 signature over them. A test vector file, docs/witness_vectors.json, holds fixed keys, requests, the exact bytes and the expected signatures, so a second implementation proves it builds the same bytes; the tests here check it, and docs/verify_witness.py checks a receipt offline with V3's public key alone.

THE RULES: an unregistered store is refused and nothing is written. A bad signature, a field outside its form, an unknown key in the body, or a body over 4 KB is refused and nothing is written. A seq V3 has not witnessed for that store is witnessed, whatever its place, since a store may send an older checkpoint after a newer one. The same seq with the same head and at returns the stored receipt unchanged, so a retry is safe. The same seq with a different head is a conflict: V3 answers 409 with the receipt it already gave, never replaces it, and keeps the conflicting request in the store's conflict file, because a second head for one sequence is evidence the chain was rewritten. At most one checkpoint per second per store is taken; more are refused with 429 and written nowhere.

THE STORE: each store has an append-only file of receipts, one JSON line each, and a conflict file, both under the data directory's attest folder; the registry is a JSON file there too. Appends are made under a lock shared across threads and processes, written whole and flushed to disk before the answer goes out, so a receipt V3 has given is a receipt V3 has kept. A line that does not parse, or a chain whose prev links do not hold, makes the store's reads and writes refuse with 503 and say so, never guess. The door runs in the front, uses no sympy and no cell, and touches no verifier.

NOT PUBLIC, NOT A SEAL: a witness receipt is not a seal. It enters no CAS, no ledger, no receipt card and no /seals listing, and it is never sent to Rekor, whatever CONCORDANCE_PUBLISH says, since the box publishes seals by default. Publication to a public log is not built in this run. GET /attest routes read files and write nothing, and a test pins that a read changes no file, the registry included.

REGISTRATION: python -m concordance attest register <store> <public_key> and attest unregister <store> edit the registry, refuse a name or key outside its form, refuse to register a name twice, and say what they did. On the box the lead runs them, on the owner's word, as the one touch outside install.sh, and the record says so. Unregistering keeps the store's receipts; it only stops new ones.

TESTS: a test registers a store with a fixed key, sends a checkpoint, and checks the receipt's bytes, hash and signature against the vectors; a retry returns the same receipt; a conflict answers 409, keeps the first receipt and writes the conflict; an unregistered store, a bad signature, each malformed field, an unknown key, an oversized body and a second checkpoint inside a second each refuse and leave every file as it was; two threads sending the same seq at once give one receipt; a store file with a broken line or a broken prev answers 503; GET reads write nothing; docs/verify_witness.py accepts a good receipt and refuses one with any byte changed. The Rekor path is shown never to be reached, with the publish setting on.

SHIP AND LIVE: after the checker's pass, the commit, the push and green CI on the branch and on main, the lead runs deploy/install.sh at that sha through the sha-checked launcher, on the owner's standing word for V3 ships. A checker then reads the live side: GET /attest/key answers V3's kid, which must equal the kid /capabilities gives for seals; GET /attest/<store>/<seq> for an unknown store answers 404; a POST from an unregistered store is refused, and the lead confirms on the box, read-only, that it wrote nothing. The first registered store is the owner's own system, registered when that system's side is built, and its first live receipt is checked then, offline, with docs/verify_witness.py.

NAMED: a receipt proves V3 saw that head at that sequence at that time; it says nothing about what the records under it hold, and a chain rewritten before its first witnessed checkpoint is not caught. It is only as strong as V3's key: a stolen key could forge receipts, which the record names as a want for key rotation and a second witness. The store's key lives with the store; a stolen store key lets a thief send heads in its name, which a conflict at an already witnessed seq still exposes.
goal: V3 becomes a witness any append-only log can use. A system that keeps a hash chain of its own records, such as an operations log or a ledger, sends V3 its chain's head from time to time, signed with its own key; V3 checks the signature, keeps a copy, and answers with a receipt signed by V3's key. Later, anyone holding that receipt and V3's public key can prove V3 saw that head at that sequence at that time, with no call to V3, and a rewrite of the chain inside the system's own database cannot forge it. This is infrastructure, not a feature of one product: the door is generic, and the first system to use it is the owner's own. The owner chose it on 2026-11-09: the public V3 as witness, publication to the public log off, and 'We want to establish it as infrastructure'.

Every pattern is matched against the whole string with nothing allowed after it, a trailing LF included. The request is a JSON object with exactly the keys store, seq, head, at, sig; sig is base64url with no padding and must re-encode to exactly the same text, which is 86 characters for 64 bytes. The store signs with Ed25519 the UTF-8 bytes 'concordance-notary-request/v1' LF store LF seq LF head LF at LF. store fully matches [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{2,62}; seq is a JSON integer, never a boolean, float or string, from 1 to 2**53-1, written in the bytes in decimal with no sign or leading zero; head fully matches [0-9a-f]{64}; at fully matches YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ and parses as a real UTC time. V3'S BYTES, exact.
